flashcards.back: Every transaction is recorded on at least two accounts, with total debits = total credits.

flashcards.front: Debit and credit for asset vs. liability accounts?
flashcards.back:
Assets increase on the debit side (left) and decrease on the credit side.
Liabilities and equity increase on the credit side (right) and decrease on the debit side.

flashcards.front: Expense and revenue accounts: which side increases them?
flashcards.back: Expenses increase on the debit side; revenues increase on the credit side.

Balance sheet: stock of assets, liabilities and equity at a point in time.
Income statement: flows of revenues and expenses over a period → profit or loss.
The systematic allocation of the cost of a long-lived asset over its useful life. Straight-line: (cost − residual value) / useful life per year.

quiz.question: A company buys a machine for CHF 10,000 in cash. The booking is…
quiz.explanation: One asset increases (machines, debit) and another decreases (cash, credit). The balance sheet total is unchanged.

quiz.question: Total assets are CHF 500k and liabilities CHF 320k. Equity is…
A machine costs 50,000, has a residual value of 10,000 and a useful life of 4 years. Annual straight-line depreciation?
Which statement shows revenues and expenses for a period?
quiz.explanation: The income statement (P&L) shows flows over a period; the balance sheet is a snapshot at a date.
